report:
I have enough evidence from major cancer bodies, prospective cohort data, and the 2004 Lancet reanalysis, along with the counter-arguments from advocacy groups pushing the ABC link.

## Report

The claim that abortion causes breast cancer is **not supported by the weight of scientific evidence** and is rejected by major medical and cancer authorities. Prospective cohort studies—considered more reliable than retrospective case-control studies—consistently find no association. A large, high-quality Finnish nationwide registry study found no increased risk of pre- or postmenopausal breast cancer linked to induced abortion or miscarriage (odds ratio ~1.01) (obgyn.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/aogs.70154). The landmark 2004 Lancet collaborative reanalysis pooled data from 53 studies across 16 countries (83,000 women with breast cancer) and found no elevated risk from abortion (www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(04)15835-2/abstract). The American Cancer Society and Susan G. Komen Foundation both state current evidence shows no causal link (www.cancer.org/cancer/risk-prevention/medical-treatments/abortion-and-breast-cancer-risk.html; www.komen.org/breast-cancer/facts-statistics/research-studies/topics/abortion-and-breast-cancer-risk/).

The historical basis for the claim comes largely from older retrospective case-control studies, which are prone to **recall bias**: healthy women may underreport past abortions, while women with breast cancer, searching for explanations, may be more likely to disclose them, artificially inflating the apparent association. Prospective studies, which avoid this bias by recording abortion history before cancer diagnosis, do not show the link. A minority of researchers (e.g., those affiliated with advocacy groups like the Breast Cancer Prevention Institute) dispute this, arguing biological plausibility and citing older studies, but their methodology has been widely criticized by mainstream epidemiologists (www.theatlantic.com/national/2013/12/inside-faulty-science-abortion-breast-cancer-link/355850/).

**Conclusion:** The scientific consensus, based on the strongest available prospective data, is that abortion does not increase breast cancer risk. The claim's persistence stems mainly from methodologically weaker retrospective studies affected by recall bias.
